rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (score 858.95, best so far). The oval finishes 20/20 in 2.12 s and the s-bend 20/20 in 2.68 s. The slalom is now the only gap: 12/20 finished, with 7 timeouts, 1 off-track exit, and a mean finish time of 2.96 s against the 3.0 s limit. The timeouts are the main failure, and the slalom is speed-limited rather than line-limited. Iteration 6 to 7 showed the same pattern: raising base_speed 1.0 to 1.1 cut slalom timeouts from 7 to 0 while the off-track count fell. Plan: raise base_speed from 1.1 to 1.25. This should bring the slalom mean time well under 3 s and turn the timeouts into finishes. The oval (2.1 s) has ample margin, so the speed rise costs little there. Other changes: none. Geometry (sensors at y=0.08, x=±0.04 at 0.02 spacing, size 0.016, track 0.11, mass 0.5) and controller (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 1.8, last_direction) stay as in iteration 8, so any shift is attributable to speed. Risks: s-bend control effort was 10.1 and line-loss events were 1.0 per run. A 14% speed rise may push the s-bend into overshoot and off-track exits. If s-bend off-track exits appear or control_effort exceeds 12, the next step is base_speed 1.18. Expected result: slalom finished count rising from 12 toward 15 to 18 out of 20, mean slalom time below 2.7 s, oval and s-bend still near 20/20. Hypotheses: H1, slalom timeouts are caused by average speed, so higher base_speed converts them to finishes. H2, the extra speed raises s-bend max_error but stays under the 0.06 m limit. Next measurements: slalom finished count, completion_time, ended_by, and s-bend max_error and control_effort to test for speed-induced overshoot.
